hint.grab: Jump towards a ledge to grab it. Push forward to climb up.
hint.push: Hold Action against a block, then push or pull.
hint.runningJump: Run for a moment before jumping to cross wide gaps.
hint.plate: Bronze plates hold their gates open only while something weighs on them.
hint.weight: The gate will not wait for you. Something heavy could keep the plate down.
hint.timer: Hear the ticking? This gate lingers a few seconds after you step off. Run.
hint.standingJump: From a standstill, a jump clears a one-block gap.
hint.fill: A block pushed into a gap drops in and becomes floor.
hint.scales: Two plates, one gate: both must bear weight at the same time.
hint.reset: If the blocks end up where they cannot help, the spring lever by the entrance puts them back.
hint.dropHang: Hold Walk and Action and step back off an edge to lower yourself and hang. Letting go from there is a shorter fall.
hint.torch: A torch. Light it at a brazier with Action; T puts it away or takes it out. With the torch in hand only one pistol is free.
hint.dark: Too dark to see the way. A lit torch would show it.
hint.carving: By torchlight, a carving on the wall: a block sliding into the chasm and becoming a bridge.
hint.temple.court: Light spills from a slit high in the north wall. The temple’s heart is up there; the way to it is not.
hint.temple.mirror: Stand against a bronze mirror and press Action to turn it a quarter turn. Follow the light.
hint.temple.twoMirrors: One mirror can hand the light on to another.
hint.temple.platform: The old stone slabs still ride their paths. Step on, stand still and let them carry you.
hint.temple.ray: A bronze ray, cut from a carved sun. Somewhere a sun is missing one.
hint.temple.run: The ceiling groans. Run, and find a way out of its path!
hint.temple.blades: The blades keep a steady beat. Wait between them, then go.
hint.temple.fire: The grates breathe fire. Embers rise and hiss just before each burst.
hint.temple.slot: The sun carved in this wall is missing a ray.
hint.temple.rays: Two sun discs flank the far gate. Both must catch the light at once.
hint.temple.guardian: Your pistols will not scratch it. The pit might hold it, or a blow from above.
hint.temple.guardian2: It will not trust the bridge again. Draw it away, climb above it and wait for its fists to strike the stone.

chambers.title: The nine chambers
chambers.lead: Eight chambers sealed with one ring, and a ninth nobody has found.
intro.antechamber.1: Eight chambers are known. Eight tombs closed with the same mark: a ring of nine segments.
intro.antechamber.2: Eight are cut into the stone. The ninth is only an outline. No one has found the chamber it stands for.
intro.antechamber.3: In 1956 the Ferrand expedition entered the tomb of Qarrum, the first chamber. Only Elena Vidal came back. She never told what she saw.
intro.antechamber.4: Seventy years on, the sand has opened the door again. Her granddaughter Nora, an archaeologist, brings Elena's notebooks and one certainty: the Amber Heart holds the first clue.
premise.antechamber: Seventy years after the Ferrand expedition, Nora Vidal opens the tomb of Qarrum to find the Amber Heart.
journal.antechamber.1.title: Day one
journal.antechamber.1.body:
We cleared the door at dawn. Above the lintel, the seal: nine segments in a ring. Eight cut deep; the ninth barely an outline, as if the mason had been told to stop.

Elena has copied it three times. She says it is not an ornament but an instruction. Hartmann has spent two rolls of film on the light that falls from the roof.

Qarrum, the first chamber. If the other seven tell the truth, the Heart is in here. We go down tomorrow.
journal.antechamber.2.meta: Fallen lintel · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.antechamber.2.title: Eight keep the way
journal.antechamber.2.body:
“Eight keep the way. One is the way.
Who carries the heart carries the light.
Let the light not return to the ninth door
until the eight have seen it.”

The last line is uncertain: the verb also allows “let the light not wake”. Grandmother copied this inscription into her notebook and wrote in the margin, underlined twice: “It is not a tomb. It is a lock.”
journal.antechamber.3.title: The slabs sing
journal.antechamber.3.body:
Ferrand will not wait. He says the pit can be cleared with a run-up and that the slabs beyond it will hold. They do not hold: they sing. Step on one and there is a thin crack, like ice, and a moment later it is gone. If they must be crossed, cross them without stopping.

Hartmann has not come back from the west ledge.

If someone finds this page: the Heart is not gold. It is a map. And maps are meant to be followed.

— E.
journal.antechamber.4.meta: Foot of the dais · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.antechamber.4.title: Where the water remembers
journal.antechamber.4.body:
“Here sleeps Qarrum, first keeper, who held the first light.
What he keeps points to the second.
Seek the second where the water remembers.”

Under this very line, in Grandmother's notebook, a single word in capitals: CISTERNS. I always thought it was a note from another trip. Now I know she copied it here, on her knees, from this same stone.
end.antechamber.kicker: Tomb of Qarrum · First chamber cleared
end.antechamber.1: The Amber Heart is warm in her hands, as if someone had only just let go of it.
end.antechamber.2: Inside the amber, cut by no tool she knows, a map of stars: eight points of light, and the empty place of a ninth.
end.antechamber.3: On the dais, scratched with a steel point, not a chisel: E. V. — 1956.
end.antechamber.figure: Star map carved inside the Amber Heart: eight stars and an empty ninth place
kicker.cisterns: Beneath the tomb of Qarrum · Second chamber
premise.cisterns: Below the tomb lie the flooded halls where Ferrand disappeared, and the second keeper’s relic.
intro.cisterns.1: Beneath the tomb of Qarrum, the water has waited three thousand years. The builders called it the mountain’s memory.
intro.cisterns.2: In 1956 Auguste Ferrand came down here alone, following the missing star. He never climbed back up.
intro.cisterns.3: Nora carries the Amber Heart. In the dark water, its light is the only thing that moves.
journal.cisterns.1.title: Last entry
journal.cisterns.1.body:
Elena will not come down. She says the Heart must stay where it is, that it is not ours to carry. She has not seen what I have seen.

The water here is not still. Twice a day it rises through the channels and falls again, like breathing. The builders wanted it so.

I have the rubbing of the star. If the second keeper answers, I will know where the ninth sleeps. If not, let whoever finds this know that I went on.
journal.cisterns.2.meta: Water gate · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.cisterns.2.title: The mountain’s memory
journal.cisterns.2.body:
“Here Nahrem, second keeper, keeps what the water remembers.
Count the faces of the moon. One is missing.
On that night the ninth door breathes.”

They counted nine faces of the moon, and the missing one is the new moon: the one night dark enough to see every star. The Heart’s map and this gate say the same thing.
journal.cisterns.3.meta: Page held down by a stone · E. Vidal · 19 March 1956
journal.cisterns.3.title: To Auguste
journal.cisterns.3.body:
Auguste:

I have waited two days by the stair. The water has risen four times and fallen four times, and you have not come back.

I am going up for help. If you return, the Heart is where we found it. I put it back. It is not ours.

— E.
kicker.sun_temple: The mountain of Qarrum · Third chamber
premise.sun_temple: High in the mountain, bronze mirrors carry the sun to a temple that is still guarded.
intro.sun_temple.1: Above the cisterns the mountain opens to the sky. Its builders brought the sun inside with mirrors of polished bronze.
intro.sun_temple.2: In the cisterns Nora found Ferrand’s satchel. The last page of his notebook is a drawing: a disc of rays, and beside it a figure of stone.
intro.sun_temple.3: The third keeper’s temple is not a tomb. Something in it has never stopped keeping watch.
journal.sun_temple.1.meta: Mirror plinth · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.sun_temple.1.title: The ray that is not cut
journal.sun_temple.1.body:
“Ubara, third keeper, holds the sun on its road.
Turn the bronze to the light and the light will find the door.
Eight rays for the eight. The ninth is not cut:
it falls where the sun sets on the longest day.”

The longest day is the summer solstice. The missing ray is not a time. It is a direction.
journal.sun_temple.2.meta: Carved on the guardian’s pedestal · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.sun_temple.2.title: The test
journal.sun_temple.2.body:
“Who comes without the heart, the stone will stop.
Who comes with it, the stone will test.”

The guardian is not protecting the temple. It is protecting the way on.
journal.sun_temple.3.meta: Folded letter behind a mirror · E. Vidal · 1989
journal.sun_temple.3.title: To whoever carries the Heart
journal.sun_temple.3.body:
I came back, thirty-three years later. The mirrors still turn; the guardian still walks. I did not bring the Heart: it was never mine, and without it the doors further on stay shut.

Three things open the ninth: the star, the night without a moon, the ray that is not cut. They rarely come together. I have counted: not in the years I have left.

If you carry the Heart, you have come further than Auguste. Do not go on alone.

— E. V.
relic.antechamber.clue: A map of stars: eight points of light and the empty place of a ninth. Where to look in the sky.
relic.cisterns.name: The Tide Glass
relic.cisterns.clue: The faces of the moon: eight carved, the ninth dark. The ninth door opens on a night without a moon.
relic.sun_temple.name: The Sun Disc
relic.sun_temple.clue: Nine rays, eight cut: the ninth falls where the sun sets on the longest day. Which way to walk.
end.cisterns.kicker: Beneath the tomb of Qarrum · Second chamber cleared
end.cisterns.1: The Tide Glass is cold, and heavier than crystal should be. Water moves inside it that no one poured.
end.cisterns.2: Held to the Heart’s light it shows the faces of the moon: eight, cut one after another, and the dark place of a ninth.
end.cisterns.3: A star and a night. Somewhere above, the mountain is waiting for both.
end.cisterns.figure: The faces of the moon inside the Tide Glass: eight carved and a dark ninth
teaser.cisterns: Above the water, the mountain opens to the sky.
end.sun_temple.kicker: The mountain of Qarrum · Third chamber cleared
end.sun_temple.1: The Sun Disc is warm on one face and cold on the other, as if it were still turning towards a sun.
end.sun_temple.2: Nine rays are marked on its rim. Eight are cut. The ninth is a line of light where no tool ever touched the metal.
end.sun_temple.3: A star, a night, a direction. Nora spreads out Elena’s notebooks and, for the first time, marks the ninth point on the map.
end.sun_temple.figure: The rim of the Sun Disc: eight cut rays and an uncut ninth
teaser.sun_temple: The ninth point is on the map. Between Nora and it, five doors that have not opened in three thousand years.
campaign.title: The Nine Chambers
chamber.1.line: The tomb of Qarrum, first keeper: sand, a shaft of daylight and the Amber Heart.
chamber.2.line: Flooded halls under the tomb, where the water rises and falls like breathing.
chamber.3.line: Bronze mirrors carry the sun into the mountain. Its keeper still keeps watch.
chamber.4.name: The Clay Archive
chamber.4.line: Ten thousand tablets, and a keeper who wrote everything down.
chamber.5.name: The Root Halls
chamber.5.line: A buried forest has grown through the stone and split it open.
chamber.6.name: The Bronze Forge
chamber.6.line: Where the builders cast their seals. The channels of fire are cold. Not all of them.
chamber.7.name: The Wind Stair
chamber.7.line: A shaft through the whole mountain that sings when the wind crosses it.
chamber.8.name: The Observatory
chamber.8.line: The last known chamber: a dome cut to watch the stars. Its door has never been opened.
chamber.9.name: The Ninth Chamber
chamber.9.line: No one has found it. No one agrees that it exists.

options.title: Options
options.quality.high.hint: Volumetric sun shafts, ambient occlusion, shadows from the nearest fires, depth of field in focus shots.
options.quality.medium.hint: One live shadow at a time, simulated light shafts, bloom and SMAA. For laptops.
options.quality.mobile.hint: Contact shadow for Nora, fewer particles, lower resolution. For phones and tablets.
options.renderer.hint: Both draw on the graphics card. WebGPU is newer and often faster; WebGL 2 works everywhere. Changing it reloads the game.
options.resolution.auto.hint: Sharp by default; lowers the resolution for a moment when the frame rate drops.
options.resolution.native.hint: The screen's full sharpness, never lowered. The most demanding.
options.resolution.scaled.hint: Fewer pixels for a steadier frame rate and a cooler battery.
options.filtering.hint: Keeps floors and walls crisp in the distance and at grazing angles.
options.sharpen.hint: A light pass that restores detail when the image is drawn below the screen's resolution.
options.stats.hint: Shows the renderer (WebGPU or WebGL 2), frame rate and resolution in a corner.
options.playtest.hint: Sessions recorded: {count}. The log stays on this device: export it to send it if you want to.
options.playtest.clear.confirm: Press again to delete every recorded session.
options.reducedMotion.hint: Removes film grain, camera sway and animated titles.
options.subtitles.hint: Captions for important sounds, with the side they come from.
hint.cisterns.start: The stair leads down into the cisterns. Where the water is shallow, wade on.
hint.cisterns.wade: Water slows you down. Where it is deeper than your chest, you swim.
hint.cisterns.swim: Swim across the cistern. Face a low edge and press Jump, or hold Action, to climb out.
hint.cisterns.dive: Hold Walk to dive and Jump to rise. Your breath will not last forever: surface where the ceiling opens.
hint.cisterns.air: Air pockets break up the drowned gallery. Surface in them to breathe.
hint.cisterns.gate: This sluice raises and lowers the water. At each level, different edges come within reach.
hint.cisterns.fall: The water is low now. Deep water breaks a fall from any height.
hint.cisterns.flares: Flares: press Flare (G, d-pad left) to light one, press again to throw it; with Walk, drop it.
hint.cisterns.braziers: The hall is cold and dark. A burning flare brought close lights a brazier.
hint.cisterns.tide: The Tide Glass rests where the water cannot reach it. Somewhere below, the tide can be turned.
seal.label: The seal of nine segments
seal.whisper: Eight are carved. The ninth is written in light.
inventory.title: Inventory
item.medkit_small.desc: Heals a little. H, or the medkit button.
item.medkit_large.desc: Heals fully. H, or the medkit button: the small one goes first when it is enough.
item.flare.desc: Press Flare to light one, again to throw it. A burning flare brought close lights a brazier.
item.torch.desc: T lights it, puts it away or takes it out. It lights the dark.
item.bronze_ray.desc: A bronze ray from the sun's disc. It fits the empty slot in the wall where the sun should strike.
options.bind.key: Press the new key (Esc to cancel). A key another action uses swaps with it.
options.bind.pad: Press the new button (Start to cancel). A button another action uses swaps with it.
hints.antechamber.lever_door.1: That north door was built to open from somewhere higher. The ledge on the west side looks important.
hints.antechamber.lever_door.2: There's a lever up on the west ledge. Too high to reach in one go, unless something gave me a step.
hints.antechamber.lever_door.3: Push the block against the west ledge, climb onto it and up, then pull the lever to open the door.
hints.antechamber.weights.1: The gate only holds while the plate is pressed. I can't stand on it and walk through at the same time.
hints.antechamber.weights.2: Something heavy in this hall could keep the plate down for me.
hints.antechamber.weights.3: Push the block onto the plate. While it weighs on it, the gate stays open: walk through.
hints.antechamber.hourglass.1: The plate at the far end keeps that gate open for a few heartbeats after I step off.
hints.antechamber.hourglass.2: Learn the jumps on the way there. The way back has to be run without a single stop.
hints.antechamber.hourglass.3: Walk the course south to the plate, step on it, then run straight back north and jump each gap without stopping.
hints.antechamber.well.1: The light comes from the top of the well. The ledges spiral up, but the first one is out of reach.
hints.antechamber.well.2: The block down here could be the first step of the climb.
hints.antechamber.well.3: Push the block west against the wall, climb onto it, and follow the ledges round and up towards the light.
hints.antechamber.causeway.1: The chasm is too wide to jump from here. That carving on the wall is trying to tell me something.
hints.antechamber.causeway.2: A block that slides into the gap drops in and becomes floor. Then the jump is short enough.
hints.antechamber.causeway.3: Push the block north into the socket at the edge, then take a run and jump the rest of the chasm.
hints.antechamber.scales.1: Two plates and one gate. Both need weight at the same time, and I am only one.
hints.antechamber.scales.2: One block can lift me to the shelf where the second one waits. After that, it can still be useful.
hints.antechamber.scales.3: The first block is my step to the shelf. Push the second onto its plate, then pull the first onto the other.
hints.antechamber.descent.1: Jumping down from here would hurt. There must be a gentler way.
hints.antechamber.descent.2: If I hang from the edge first, the drop is much shorter.
hints.antechamber.descent.3: Lower myself carefully over the edge, hang, and let go. Twice, and I am down without a scratch.
hints.cisterns.sluice.1: This sluice moves the water up and down. Every level brings different edges within reach.
hints.cisterns.sluice.2: The door's lever is in the basin, reachable only with the water low. The door itself needs high water.
hints.cisterns.sluice.3: Lower the water, pull the door lever in the basin, raise the water again and swim to the open door.
hints.cisterns.dark.1: The grate stays shut while this hall is cold. Those braziers have not burned in decades.
hints.cisterns.dark.2: Ferrand's flares could do it. Each cold brazier needs a burning flare brought close.
hints.cisterns.dark.3: Light a flare and carry it to each of the three cold braziers. When all three burn, the grate opens.
hints.cisterns.tide.1: The Tide Glass sits above the water, out of reach. The water here must be able to rise.
hints.cisterns.tide.2: Under the arch there is a cave, and in it something that turns the tide.
hints.cisterns.tide.3: Dive under the arch to the cave, pull the tide lever, swim back and let the risen water carry you up.
hints.sun_temple.mirror_a.1: The sun falls on that bronze mirror. The disc over the gate is waiting for its light.
hints.sun_temple.mirror_a.2: The mirror turns, a quarter at a time. I have to follow where the light lands.
hints.sun_temple.mirror_a.3: Turn the first mirror a quarter at a time until its beam strikes the disc above the gate.
hints.sun_temple.mirror_b.1: The second gate has its own disc, and no sunlight reaches it directly.
hints.sun_temple.mirror_b.2: One mirror can hand the light on to another.
hints.sun_temple.mirror_b.3: Aim one mirror's beam at the next mirror, then turn that one until the light reaches the second gate's disc.
hints.sun_temple.lift.1: The gallery is far above. These old slabs still travel up and down the shaft.
hints.sun_temple.lift.2: If I stand still on a slab, it will carry me. The waiting is the hard part.
hints.sun_temple.lift.3: Step onto the moving slab, stay still while it rises, and step off at the gallery above.
hints.sun_temple.sun_slot.1: The sun carved on this wall is missing one ray. The door won't open while it is incomplete.
hints.sun_temple.sun_slot.2: I saw a loose bronze ray in the vault, before the boulder.
hints.sun_temple.sun_slot.3: Bring the bronze ray from the vault and set it in the empty slot of the carved sun.
hints.sun_temple.rays.1: Two discs flank the far gate. One lit is not enough: both must catch the light together.
hints.sun_temple.rays.2: The mirrors here can't be reached from the floor. The moving platform passes close to both.
hints.sun_temple.rays.3: Ride the shuttle and turn each mirror from it until both discs are lit at the same time.
hints.sun_temple.guardian.1: My pistols don't even scratch it. It is stone; something heavier than a bullet has to stop it.
hints.sun_temple.guardian.2: That bridge can drop. And once it has learned, its own fists striking hard stone below me might break it.
hints.sun_temple.guardian.3: Lure it onto the bridge and pull the lever. When it climbs out, get above it and let its slam strike stone.
hint.offer: Nora has an idea. Pause to hear it.
hint.title: Nora's idea
kicker.clay_archive: Beneath the Temple of the Sun · Fourth chamber
premise.clay_archive: Under the temple, ten thousand clay tablets keep the names of the eight, and the word that opens the ninth.
intro.clay_archive.1: Under the Temple of the Sun the rock was cut into shelves, and the shelves were filled with clay.
intro.clay_archive.2: Tamrit, the fourth keeper, wrote everything down: the eight, their builders, and the name of the ninth.
intro.clay_archive.3: No one has opened these doors in three thousand years. The dust has kept the silence.
relic.clay_archive.name: The Tablet of the Name
relic.clay_archive.clue: Nine columns of signs: eight names, and a ninth that is a single sign. The word that opens the ninth.
end.clay_archive.kicker: Beneath the Temple of the Sun · Fourth chamber cleared
end.clay_archive.1: The Tablet of the Name is fired clay, lighter than it looks, still warm from the kiln it never left.
end.clay_archive.2: Eight columns are names. The ninth holds one sign, pressed so deep that light gathers in it.
end.clay_archive.3: Where, when, which way, and now what to say at the door. Four of the five doors are left.
end.clay_archive.figure: The Tablet of the Name: eight columns of signs and a single ninth sign
teaser.clay_archive: Below the archive, roots have split the rock. Something there is still growing.
journal.clay_archive.1.meta: Relief over the reading room · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.clay_archive.1.title: The one who wrote
journal.clay_archive.1.body:
“Tamrit, fourth keeper, wrote all that was.
Before the names, before the doors, he wrote the first thing:
the water that came down from the mountain.
His door wakes for it.”

The cylinder by the door has six signs. One of them is water.
journal.clay_archive.2.meta: Broken tablet in the dark gallery · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.clay_archive.2.title: The names of the eight
journal.clay_archive.2.body:
A list, and each name with its sign:

“Qarrum, the first: the star.
Nahrem, who drowned the halls: the water.
Ubara, who keeps the sun: the sun.
Tamrit, who wrote: the reed.”

Four more lines are broken off. Where the ninth should be, the clay was left smooth.
journal.clay_archive.3.meta: Tablet set above the ninth door's model · Translated by N. Vidal
journal.clay_archive.3.title: The word without sound
journal.clay_archive.3.body:
“The name of the ninth is not spoken.
It is written in the stone with light:
where to look, when to come, which way to walk.”

The star, the night without a moon, the ray. I already carry all three. In this archive, a night without a moon is written as water.
hint.archive.start: The archive under the temple: dry, silent and dark. The dust swallows every step.
hint.archive.lock: A stone cylinder carved with six signs. Action turns it one sign on; the carving nearby says which sign it waits for.
hint.archive.shelves: These shelves were cut loose from the rock. They can be pushed, and pulled.
hint.archive.darts: Painted slabs, and small holes in the walls. Something waits for whoever lingers on them.
hint.archive.kiln: Carved over the kiln: “The first keeper, then the one who wrote.”
hint.archive.index: Carved between the cylinders: “On the left hand, the one who drowned the halls; on the right, the one who keeps the sun.”
hint.archive.canal: This sluice feeds the halls beyond. Whatever opens it is not here.
hint.archive.tamrit: It rises again however often it falls. Clay fears only water.
hint.archive.name: Above the three cylinders: “Look. Come. Walk.”
hints.clay_archive.reading.1: The cylinder waits for one sign. The relief on the north wall talks about the first thing Tamrit wrote.
hints.clay_archive.reading.2: The first thing written was the water that came down from the mountain.
hints.clay_archive.reading.3: Turn the cylinder from its east side until it shows water: the blue waves.
hints.clay_archive.stacks.1: The way north is blocked by a shelf in the gap of the wall.
hints.clay_archive.stacks.2: The shelves move like blocks. That one could go further north, out of the way.
hints.clay_archive.stacks.3: Stand south of the shelf in the gap and push it north twice, then walk through.
hints.clay_archive.darts.1: Those painted slabs click when I step on them. A moment later, something flies across.
hints.clay_archive.darts.2: The click gives me a heartbeat. If I don't stop, I'm past before the darts come.
hints.clay_archive.darts.3: Run over each painted slab without stopping. If a dart hits, a medkit cures the poison.
hints.clay_archive.kiln.1: The kiln's mouth stays shut, and inside two cylinders wait for the first keeper and the one who wrote.
hints.clay_archive.kiln.2: A weight on the plate holds the mouth open. The broken tablet named each keeper's sign.
hints.clay_archive.kiln.3: Push the block onto the plate. Inside, set the left cylinder to the star and the right one to the reed.
hints.clay_archive.index.1: Two cylinders, two keepers named by what they did. The broken tablet gave their signs.
hints.clay_archive.index.2: The one who drowned the halls was Nahrem, and Ubara keeps the sun.
hints.clay_archive.index.3: Set the left cylinder to the water and the right one to the sun.
hints.clay_archive.tamrit.1: Bullets break it, but it always rises again. There must be something clay can't survive.
hints.clay_archive.tamrit.2: That sluice in the canal feeds this hall. The lever must be up on the ledge, out of its reach.
hints.clay_archive.tamrit.3: Climb the steps to the ledge, pull the lever and let the water rise over Tamrit.
hints.clay_archive.name.1: Three cylinders: look, come, walk. The last tablet says the word is written with light.
hints.clay_archive.name.2: Where to look, when to come, which way to walk: the three relics I already carry.
hints.clay_archive.name.3: From left to right: the star, the water for the moonless night, and the sun.
options.trapCues.hint: An arrow at the edge of the screen points at a trap that has just armed.
options.gameSpeed.hint: Slows the whole game down. Times and records are not affected.
options.highContrast.hint: Draws a bright line along every edge Nora can grab.
options.colourSafe.hint: Health and poison in blue and orange, with stripes for poison.
